snippets.title: Configure the RevenueDot iOS SDK
snippets.notes: Install the RevenueDot SDK with Swift Package Manager (https://github.com/revenuedot/purchases-ios, exact version 5.91.0-revenuedot, product RevenueCat) or CocoaPods (pod 'RevenueDotPurchases', '5.91.0'). It needs no RevenueCat account. Self-hosting: set Purchases.proxyURL = URL(string: "https://your-server")! before configure and use .with(entitlementVerificationMode: .disabled), because your server signs with its own key. An app that already ships the RevenueCat SDK keeps it, sets Purchases.proxyURL to https://api.revenuedot.app before configure and turns verification off (see https://revenuedot.app/docs/migrate).

snippets.title: Configure the RevenueDot Android SDK
snippets.notes: Install the RevenueDot SDK from Maven Central: implementation("app.revenuedot.purchases:purchases:10.23.3"). The Kotlin packages stay com.revenuecat.purchases.*, and it sends diagnostics and paywall events to RevenueDot too. Self-hosting: set Purchases.proxyURL = URL("https://your-server") before configure and use EntitlementVerificationMode.DISABLED; the emulator reaches your computer at http://10.0.2.2:8787. An app that already ships the RevenueCat SDK keeps it and sets the proxy URL to https://api.revenuedot.app (see https://revenuedot.app/docs/migrate).

snippets.title: Configure the RevenueDot SDK for React Native and Expo
snippets.notes: The npm alias installs the RevenueDot SDK under the name react-native-purchases, so imports stay the same. In Expo Go and on the web the SDK only accepts a Test Store key (test_...); real store purchases need a development build (expo run:ios or expo run:android). Self-hosting: await Purchases.setProxyURL("https://your-server") before configure. An app that already ships RevenueCat's react-native-purchases keeps it and awaits setProxyURL("https://api.revenuedot.app") before configure (see https://revenuedot.app/docs/migrate).

snippets.title: Configure the RevenueDot Flutter SDK
snippets.notes: Install the RevenueDot SDK as a git dependency in pubspec.yaml: purchases_flutter: { git: { url: https://github.com/revenuedot/purchases-flutter.git, ref: 10.13.2-revenuedot } }. The pub.dev name belongs to RevenueCat, so it is not on pub.dev; imports stay package:purchases_flutter. It also works on Flutter web. Self-hosting: await Purchases.setProxyURL('https://your-server') before configure. An app that already ships RevenueCat's purchases_flutter keeps it and sets the proxy URL to https://api.revenuedot.app (see https://revenuedot.app/docs/migrate).

snippets.title: Show the current offering, buy a package and check the pro entitlement (iOS)
snippets.notes: Check an entitlement ('pro'), never a product id, so adding a plan later needs no app update. A cancelled purchase is a normal result, not an error.

snippets.title: Buy a package and check the pro entitlement (React Native and Expo)
snippets.notes: A cancelled purchase sets userCancelled on the error. Offer Restore with Purchases.restorePurchases().

snippets.title: Buy a package and check the pro entitlement (Android, coroutines)
snippets.notes: Needs the purchases coroutine helpers and an Activity for the purchase sheet.

snippets.title: Verify a RevenueDot webhook signature on the raw body (Node.js)
snippets.notes: Pass the raw request bytes, not re-serialized JSON. The header is X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature. Answer 200 fast and ignore an event.id you have already handled. Load the signing secret from your backend's secret store, never from the app.

snippets.title: Store-native: buy, read entitlements and restore with StoreKit 2
snippets.notes: Store-native means you verify transactions and track renewals yourself, usually with the App Store Server API and App Store Server Notifications V2 (signed JWS payloads). Product ids must match App Store Connect exactly. Written from Apple's API names; not compiled in this repository.

snippets.title: Store-native: acknowledge a verified Google Play purchase
snippets.notes: Never grant access while the state is PENDING. Call queryPurchasesAsync on launch and when the app returns to the foreground. A backend should acknowledge from the server for better security.
